15Glossary

ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVW
A
AF allele frequency
Fraction of reads at a site carrying the alternate allele. In the report this is the raw, uncorrected value; the purity- and ploidy-adjusted equivalent is variant copy number. See small variants.
Allelic imbalance
Unequal representation of the two parental alleles at a locus. Detected via BAF deviating from 0.5, and quantified by MACN.
AMBER
hmftools component that generates the tumor BAF file at germline heterozygous sites for PURPLE's copy number fit, and detects contamination. Docs
AMP / DEL / HET_DEL / LOH
Copy number event types in the amplifications & deletions table: amplification, homozygous deletion, heterozygous deletion, and copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity.
Aneuploidy
Departure from an integer-balanced diploid karyotype. The pattern of aneuploidy is what allows PURPLE to fit purity and ploidy jointly; samples with little aneuploidy fall back to the SOMATIC fit method.
APOBEC
Family of cytidine deaminases acting on single-stranded DNA, producing C>T and C>G changes in a TpCpN context. The mechanism behind kataegis and COSMIC signatures 2 and 13.
Arm CN
Mean copy number of the chromosome arm containing a gene. Comparing it against the gene's REL CN distinguishes focal from arm-level events. See arm copy number.
B
BAF B-allele frequency
At a germline heterozygous SNP, the fraction of reads carrying the "B" allele — 0.5 in normal diploid tissue. Deviation reveals allelic imbalance even when total copy number is unchanged, which is what makes copy-neutral LOH detectable. Measured by AMBER. See the input CIRCOS.
Biallelic
Both copies of a gene affected, so no wildtype allele remains. Reported as a probability derived from copy number and purity. Decisive for tumor suppressors (Knudson's two-hit model) and it changes the driver likelihood calculation. See biallelic likelihood.
BND
Structural variant type: a breakend pair joining two different chromosomes — a translocation.
BQR base quality recalibration
Adjustment of variant base qualities to correct sequencer-specific biases. + = quality boosted, − = quality reduced. See the BQR plots.
Breakend / breakpoint
A breakend is one side of a structural variant junction; a breakpoint is the junction itself. A single breakend with no resolvable partner is typed SGL.
C
Chimeric rate
RNA QC metric: proportion of genic fragments whose other splice site is inverted, inter-chromosomal, or more than 500 kb away. See RNA QC.
CHORD
Logistic-regression classifier predicting HR deficiency from indel and SV signatures in WGS. Score 0–1; >0.5 is HRD-positive. The panel equivalent is vCHORD. Docs
CIRCOS
Circular whole-genome plot with one concentric ring per event class: chromosomes, SNVs, INDELs, copy number, MACN, and structural variants at the centre. See the CIRCOS guide.
Cis-phased
Two variants on the same physical allele. Marked with an asterisk on the position. Two truncating variants in trans inactivate both copies; in cis they leave one intact.
ClinVar
NCBI archive of submitted clinical variant interpretations, surfaced in the germline small variants table. An aggregation of others' assertions, not an independent Hartwig classification. ClinVar
Clonal / subclonal
Clonal = present in essentially every tumor cell (an early event). Subclonal = present in only a fraction (a later event in one lineage). Determined by peak fitting in the variant copy number distribution; peaks below 0.85 copies are subclonal.
COBALT
hmftools component computing GC-normalised read depth ratios for PURPLE's copy number fit. Docs
Cohort frequency
Number of observations of an RNA fusion or splice junction across the Hartwig WTS cohort. High values usually indicate a recurrent artefact or unannotated normal transcript rather than a private driver.
Consensus read
A single read synthesised from PCR duplicates of one original molecule. Types: NONE (no deduplication), SINGLE (one strand), DUAL (both strands). DUAL support is the strongest evidence, because single-strand damage artefacts such as FFPE deamination do not appear on both strands. Produced by REDUX.
COSMIC
Catalogue of Somatic Mutations in Cancer. The report uses the v2 SBS signature catalogue (signatures 1–30); COSMIC's live site is at v3.x, so numbering will not match. v2 archive
CUPPA
Cancer of Unknown Primary Prediction Algorithm — predicts tissue of origin from WGS(+WTS) features using per-feature logistic regressions (GEN_POS, SNV96, EVENT, GENE_EXP, ALT_SJ). WGS only. See tissue of origin.
D
Depth ratio
GC- and enrichment-normalised read depth divided by the sample's mean depth. The primary copy number signal, computed by COBALT. See input CIRCOS.
Discordant fragment
A read pair whose orientation or spacing departs from expectation. Not necessarily evidence of a structural variant — read as a library-quality metric. See QC plots.
dN/dS
Ratio of non-synonymous to synonymous mutation rates. An excess of non-synonymous change indicates positive selection, and is the statistical basis of driver likelihood for non-hotspot variants. Trained on the Hartwig WGS pan-cancer cohort — adult solid tumors only.
DPYD
Gene encoding dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase, which clears fluoropyrimidines (5-FU, capecitabine). Reduced-function haplotypes carry substantial toxicity risk. Currently the only gene in the pharmacogenetics table.
Driver gene panel
Configuration file (DriverGenePanel.{37,38}.tsv) listing reportable genes with per-variant-type flags, the ONCO/TSG classification, and optional per-gene amplification thresholds. Drives report content and driver likelihood calibration. See configuration.
Driver likelihood
Estimate between 0 and 1 that a variant is a driver. Hotspots, biallelic nonsense/splice in TSGs, and in-frame indels outside repeats in oncogenes get 1; the rest are scored from dN/dS excess and a TMB-aware Bayesian model. Values <20% render on a grey background. See the model.
DUP / DEL / INV
Structural variant types: tandem duplication, deletion, inversion.
E
ESVEE
Current hmftools structural variant caller (assembly-based), feeding PURPLE and LINX. Docs
EVENT classifier
CUPPA DNA classifier using cancer-type-specific mutational events — driver mutations, fusions, viral insertions. Its contributions are shown as odds ratios.
EXON_DEL_DUP
Curated pathogenic exon deletion or duplication in the fusion knowledgebase. Also the reportability criterion for novel splice junctions.
F
FFPE
Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue. Fixation fragments DNA and causes cytosine deamination, producing artefactual C>T changes — which is why DUAL consensus read support and the fragment length plot matter for FFPE inputs.
Fit method
How purity and ploidy were determined: NORMAL (from aneuploidy — preferred), SOMATIC (ploidy assumed 2, purity from somatic variant AFs), or NO_TUMOR. See sample details.
Focal vs arm-level
A focal copy number event is localised and stands out against its arm baseline — more likely selected. An arm-level event carries many genes along passively. Compare REL CN with ARM CN.
Fusion
Juxtaposition of two genes by a structural rearrangement, potentially producing a chimeric transcript. Typed KNOWN_PAIR, KNOWN_ENHANCER_PAIR, KNOWN_EXON_DEL_DUP, or PROMISCUOUS_3/5. See fusions.
G
GC bias
Depth variation driven by local base composition rather than true copy number. Corrected by COBALT; the residual is plotted in QC.
GEN_POS
CUPPA DNA classifier using SNV counts in 500 kb bins. Works because mutation density tracks replication timing and chromatin state, which are cell-type specific.
gnomAD
Genome Aggregation Database — population allele frequencies, the first sanity check on any germline call. gnomAD
H
HGVS
Standard nomenclature for describing sequence variants relative to a reference transcript — the c. (coding) and p. (protein) forms in the HGVS column. Standard
HLA
Human leukocyte antigen. Class I (HLA-A, -B, -C) present antigens on all nucleated cells; Class II (here DPA1, DPB1, DQA1, DQB1) on professional antigen-presenting cells. Tumor-specific HLA loss or mutation is an immune escape mechanism. Typed by LILAC. See immunology.
Hotspot
The exact variant (chromosome, position, ref, alt) matches a curated known pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant. Automatically assigned driver likelihood 1, and treated as HIGH somatic likelihood in tumor-only mode.
HRD homologous recombination deficiency
Loss of the HR double-strand break repair pathway, often via BRCA1/2. Inferred from the genomic scar (deletions with microhomology, 1–100 kb duplications) by CHORD, not from the presence of a gene variant. See HR deficiency.
I
IMGT allele
HLA allele name such as A*11:01: gene, allele group, specific protein. Two-field resolution determines the presented peptide repertoire. IPD-IMGT/HLA
INDEL
Short insertion or deletion, <50 bp in the CIRCOS INDEL ring. Coloured yellow (insertion), red (deletion), green (deletion with microhomology).
Inframe / out-of-frame
Whether a fusion preserves the reading frame across the junction. Out-of-frame fusions are still reported because they can inactivate the 3′ gene. Skipped exons means frame is restored by omitting exons.
ISOFOX
hmftools RNA component: transcript abundance, fusion calling and novel splice junction detection. Docs
J
JCN junction copy number
Number of copies of a structural variant junction present in each tumor cell — the copy number of the junction itself, not of the flanking sequence.
Jitter
Polymerase slippage causing reads to report the wrong repeat length in microsatellites. Indistinguishable read-by-read from a real microsatellite indel, so an empirical per-sample jitter model (built by REDUX) is what makes the MSI call possible. See jitter QC plots.
K
Kataegis
Localised hypermutation: ≥3 C>T or C>G mutations in a TpCpN context on the same strand within a region averaging ≤1 kb inter-mutation distance. Caused by APOBEC activity on single-stranded DNA, usually near SV breakpoints. See kataegis plot.
Klinefelter
Constitutional sex chromosome aneuploidy (XXY), detectable in the chromosomal aberrations table and a benign explanation for WARN_GENDER_MISMATCH.
L
LILAC
hmftools component for HLA class I/II typing with allele copy number and somatic mutation detection. Docs
LINX
hmftools component that annotates, clusters and chains structural variants into events, reconstructs derivative chromosomes, and calls fusions and homozygous disruptions. Also produces the per-driver LINX plots. Docs · Guide
LOH loss of heterozygosity
Loss of one parental allele. Copy-neutral LOH (2+0) has normal total copy number and is only detectable via BAF/MACN. The route to biallelic inactivation of a tumor suppressor when combined with a variant on the other allele. Reported by default only for MMRd- and HRD-associated genes.
M
MACN minor allele copy number
Copy count of the less frequent (or lost) allele at a locus. Normal expectation is 1. Below 1 = LOH; above 1 = amplification of both alleles. Distinguishes 1+1 from 2+0, which total copy number cannot. See MACN ring.
MISALLOC
Row in the signature table counting somatic variants that could not be assigned to any known signature. A large fraction means the decomposition fit is poor.
Missed variant likelihood
QC estimate, per gene, of the probability that a variant present in the sample was not detected. Only genes above 1% are shown (up to 20). The check to run before trusting any negative finding. See QC plots.
MMR mismatch repair
DNA repair system (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) that corrects replication errors. Its failure causes microsatellite instability. See MSI.
MSI / MSS
Microsatellite instable (≥4 microsatellite indels per Mb) or stable (<4). Counted directly for WGS; estimated from panel-region repeat error rates for targeted assays. An important predictive biomarker for immunotherapy response.
N
Novel splice junction
An RNA splice junction not annotated in Ensembl. Types: MIXED_TRANSCRIPT, NOVEL_EXON, SKIPPED_EXON, NOVEL_5_PRIME_SS, NOVEL_3_PRIME_SS, INTRONIC, INTRONIC_TO_EXONIC, NOVEL_INTRON, and retained intron. Reportable when matching a curated EXON_DEL_DUP. See novel splice junctions.
O
Odds ratio CUPPA event classifier
Effect of a feature on cancer type probability: 1 = no change, >1 = increase, <1 = decrease. Ratios between two cancer types give the relative preference — e.g. BRAF 49 (melanoma) / 23 (thyroid) = 2.13× more likely melanoma.
ONCO oncogene
Driver gene panel classification for genes acting through gain of function. In-frame indels outside repeat contexts get driver likelihood 1. Contrast TSG.
ORANGE
Oncogenic Results of Analyzing the Genome — the hmftools component that assembles every upstream tool's output into a single PDF and JSON. Docs
P
PAVE
hmftools component annotating point mutations with transcript and protein impact. Docs
PDF probability density function (plots)
In the purity chapter, the CN PDF and MACN PDF show the distribution of observed copy number states weighted by BAF point count. Clear integer peaks indicate a good fit.
PEACH
hmftools component calling pharmacogenomic haplotypes from germline variants. Docs
Ploidy
Average number of copies of each chromosome in the tumor cells; 2 for a normal diploid genome. Amplification thresholds are expressed relative to it, so a whole genome duplication rescales them.
Promiscuous partner
A gene that recurs as a fusion partner with many different counterparts. Novel pairings involving one are reported (typed PROMISCUOUS_3/5) but with LOW driver likelihood, since the specific pair is uncurated.
PURPLE
The central hmftools component: fits purity, ploidy and allele-specific copy number from COBALT depth ratios and AMBER BAFs, then calls driver events. Its QC gates most of the report. Docs
Purity
Fraction of cells in the sequenced sample that are tumor cells. Below 20% (WARN_LOW_PURITY) negative findings become uninterpretable and quantitative values degrade.
Q
Qsee
hmftools component that aggregates QC metrics from PURPLE, BamTools, COBALT, ESVEE and REDUX and plots them against a reference cohort with warn/fail thresholds — it renders the QC page. Docs
Quantile CUPPA
If less than 1, the quantile within the cohort; for values above 1, the multiple of the highest cohort value.
R
REDUX
hmftools component handling duplicate marking, consensus reads, UMIs, read unmapping and the microsatellite jitter model. No section of its own, but its output determines what every caller sees. Docs
REL CN
Gene copy number relative to tumor ploidy (MIN_CN / PLOIDY). The quantity amplification and arm-level thresholds are expressed in. For male X and Y, computed relative to ploidy / 2.
S
SAGE
hmftools point mutation caller and filter; also contains the TINC module. Docs
SGL
Single breakend structural variant — only one side of the junction could be resolved.
Signature SBS
Characteristic distribution across the 96 trinucleotide substitution types left by a mutational process. Signature analysis attributes mutations to reference distributions; it does not measure exposure. Rule of thumb for significance: >20% or >2000 variants. See signatures.
SIGS
hmftools component fitting the sample's SNV trinucleotide counts to the COSMIC signature catalogue. Docs
SNV96
The 96 trinucleotide mutation contexts (6 substitution classes × 4 upstream bases × 4 downstream bases). Used by the CUPPA SNV96 classifier and in the BQR plots.
Somatic likelihood
Tumor-only Probability that a variant is somatic rather than inherited, from comparing its AF against expected germline and somatic VAFs given purity and ploidy. Reported as HIGH, MED or LOW. See the rules.
Sunrise plot
Heatmap of relative score across the full purity × ploidy solution matrix. Solutions within 10% of the best are blue and define the uncertainty range. The single best plot for judging fit confidence. See sunrise plot.
T
TINC tumor in normal contamination
Tumor DNA present in the germline reference sample. Reduces somatic sensitivity, because real somatic variants get filtered as germline. WARN above 0.5%, FAIL above 25%. Estimated within SAGE.
TMB tumor mutational burden
Density of all small variant mutations per Mb. High if ≥10. Counted directly for WGS; estimated from coding on-target regions for panels. Also modulates driver likelihood. See TMB and TML.
TML tumor mutational load
Count of somatic missense mutations genome-wide. High if ≥140. Tracks potential neoepitope supply more directly than TMB.
TPM transcripts per million
Length- and depth-normalised expression measure. Percentiles in the report are relative to the Hartwig pan-cancer WTS cohort, not a matched-tissue cohort. See high expression.
TSG tumor suppressor gene
Driver gene panel classification for genes acting through loss of function. Biallelic status is taken into account, multiple mutations give additive likelihoods, and biallelic nonsense or canonical splice variants get driver likelihood 1. Contrast ONCO.
U
UMI unique molecular identifier
Molecular barcode allowing PCR duplicates of the same original molecule to be grouped into a consensus read. Handled by REDUX.
Undisrupted CN
Number of copies of a gene unaffected by a given disruption in each tumor cell. Reaching zero means no intact copy remains — a homozygous disruption. See gene disruptions.
Unspliced rate
RNA QC metric: proportion of genic fragments supporting intronic regions, which may reflect pre-spliced transcript or DNA contamination.
V
VCN variant copy number
Number of copies of a variant allele in the average tumor cell, after purity and ploidy correction — the first number in the COPIES column. VCN below ~0.85 indicates subclonality.
vCHORD / vCUPPA
Panel-specific counterparts to CHORD and CUPPA. vCHORD is an image-based HRD classifier trained per panel; vCUPPA predicts tissue of origin for panels but is not currently surfaced in ORANGE.
VIRUSBreakend
External tool (GRIDSS suite) detecting viral presence and integration sites; results are filtered and annotated by Virus Interpreter for the virus table. Docs
W
WGD whole genome duplication
A single event doubling the entire karyotype, pushing ploidy toward 4. Rescales every ploidy-relative threshold in the report, so an absolute copy number of 2 can represent a relative loss. Reported as Whole genome duplicated on the front page.
WiGiTS
The Hartwig genomics toolkit — the current branding of the hmftools component suite. Its version is independent of the oncoanalyser pipeline version.
WTS whole transcriptome sequencing
RNA-seq of the full transcriptome. The reference cohort for RNA percentiles and cohort frequencies is the Hartwig pan-cancer WTS cohort.

ORANGE Report User Guide — compiled from the Hartwig Medical Foundation ORANGE Report user manual (HMFAUS-DOC-22 v1.0, 28 July 2026), the hmftools and oncoanalyser repositories, and the public documentation and publications listed under References.

Research Use Only. This guide is documentation, not a clinical decision aid. Verify all thresholds and behaviours against the documentation for the exact pipeline version that produced your report.
